description:
FILED s483 (Fable, 2026-09-13) from the #1592 merge-review probes.  PRE-EXISTING on main eabff00d (probed there, identical on the s483a tree cc32d64f); NOT specific to CODE -- every blessed referent shows it.

PROBE (perl 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl):
    my $b = bless sub { 11 }, 'K'; print ref(\$b), "\n";     # perl REF   PCL K
    my $h = bless {}, 'H';         print ref(\$h), "\n";     # perl REF   PCL H
    my $s = "x"; my $bs = bless \$s, 'S'; print ref(\$bs), "\n";   # perl REF   PCL S
The unblessed twin is RIGHT on main: `my $cr = sub {7}; ref(\$cr)` is REF, `my $hr = {}; ref(\$hr)` is REF.

SHAPE: `\$var` where $var HOLDS a blessed reference answers the CLASS of the held value where perl answers REF (a reference to a scalar that holds a reference).  Suspect: the ref-string/`ref` path reads the blessing off the referent one level too deep -- the same "which level is the referent" family as #1249(1)/#1592 (`%p-ref-referent`, `%p-ref-string`); the unblessed twin being right says the level is fine and the BLESS lookup is what walks through.  Cheap discriminating measurement: trace `p-ref`/`%p-ref-string` on `\$b` and see whether the class comes from the outer box or the inner.

FIX: perl's rule -- `ref` reports the blessing of the REFERENT itself, and a scalar holding a blessed ref is not blessed.  Guard rows beside #1592's in Pl/t/ref-to-ref-01.t (the three shapes above + the unblessed twins as negatives), inverse-verified.  `cl/` change -> full sweep + companion op/ref.t + op/bless.t.  SIZE: S.

=== DONE (s483b) ===
FIXED, runtime-only (no emission change, no generation bump).

CAUSE (traced, not guessed -- a box dump of the wrapper, the variable box and
the referent): a p-box's CLASS SLOT carries TWO perl facts.  (a) the CACHE of
the class of the REFERENCE the box holds -- the ONLY storage there is when the
payload is a raw ARRAY/CODE/GLOB, which is why %p-ref-shaped-p exists; and (b)
the SvSTASH that `bless \$x, "C"` writes on the SV $x itself.  Three readers
took (a) for (b):
  * %p-target-class's `((p-box-p v) (or (%p-referent-class box) (p-box-class v)))`
    -- when BOX is the is-ref WRAPPER, v is the REFERENT scalar and its slot is
    that scalar's own cache, never the class of the reference being asked about;
  * p-ref's `((p-box-p inner) (if (p-box-class inner) (p-box-class inner) ...))`
    -- the same read one layer down, and the arm that actually answered `H`;
  * p-bless's scalar-referent branch, on the WRITE side, which CLOBBERED the
    cache: `my $h = {}; bless \$h, "S"` made ref($h) answer S (perl: HASH).

FIX: the rare fact gets its own home -- `*p-sv-stash*`, a weak EQ table keyed by
the referent BOX, written only by p-bless's scalar-referent branch and read only
by %p-referent-class (guarded by a hash-table-count test, so the p-ref/box-sv hot
path pays one slot read in a program that never blesses a scalar ref).  The class
slot keeps the cache: %p-target-class reads it only when the box is NOT is-ref
(the same discriminator %p-ref-referent uses) and p-ref's arm is deleted.
p-bless writes the referent's slot only for a PLAIN-scalar payload.

RULE 11 SIBLING: p-reftype is the second reading of the same question and was
wrong in two places -- `((string= r "REF") "SCALAR")` (perl's reftype of a
ref-to-ref is REF, probed six shapes) and the blessed `(p-box-p inner)` arm,
which now asks %p-scalar-referent-p.  builtin::blessed/refaddr/reftype all
derive from p-ref, so they followed for free.

MEASURED: 38-shape battery vs perl 5.40.3 (scratch/s483b/probes/b1619.pl) -- 37
identical, incl. every negative (ref($o), the copy, the element reads, `bless $r`
not re-classing the object, "$o"/"$r" stringification, the undef/number/qr//glob
/filehandle referents).  The 38th is a PARSE bug, filed as #1620.
reftype/blessed battery (probes/reftype.pl): 15 of 15 identical.

BARS: gate 235 files / 8081 rows, xs-01/02/03 only (the 13 standing pclxs rows);
full sweep --jobs 4 GATE clean, 0 new / 0 fixed / 0 LOST, TOTAL passing 18675
(+0), drops 5 = census; companion op/ref.t 202/40 + op/bless.t 111/6 = snapshot,
ROW DIFF 0 NEW; ir-conform 321/0/24/0.  Guard Pl/t/ref-to-ref-01.t 30 -> 36,
inverse-verified on a `git archive e3767cff` extraction (rows 11, 31-33, 35 fail
there; the two negatives pass on both sides).  ONE STALE ROW repaired in the same
commit (s416 rule): `reftype($rr) is SCALAR` asserted the bug -- rewritten under
the s377 four-conjunct rule.  ir-spec 2.6 carries the normative rule.
subject: `ref(\$var)` where $var HOLDS a BLESSED reference answers the CLASS where perl answers REF (unblessed twin is right) -- pre-existing, every blessed referent
